inventory.description: One upright cylindrical jar on the left, with an elliptical open upper rim, curved lower boundary, and an exposed upper wall above the coated lower region. It is not a pair of jars or separate subfigures.

The lower jar region has a dark interior ellipse and strongly drawn lower cylindrical wall/coating boundaries. The inner and outer conducting regions are separated by the jar wall; the monochrome source does not individually label the layers or quantify their thickness.

One vertical rod descends through the open top into the dark interior conducting region. One small rounded terminal sits above the upper rim. The top terminal and lower coating connection are vertically separated.

One discharge tool to the right comprises an upper curved arm toward the top rod terminal, a lower curved arm toward the lower outer side of the jar, a common junction to the right, and one thick handle extending rightward with a slight upward slope.

Rounded contact/end regions are visible at the upper terminal and beside the jar's outer coating at the lower arm. The arm ends approach or meet the two different conductors; they do not both terminate on the central rod. Tiny exact contact gaps cannot be confidently distinguished in the coarse source.

No separate zigzag spark, lightning symbol, radiating spark burst, charge signs, or directional arrows are distinctly visible. Dark junction/contact marks must not be reclassified as a source-mandated spark.
No visible printed labels, caption, letters, numbers, units, axes, grid, measurements, equations, or answer-bearing text occur in this source crop.
